- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. The token `acsf90c0a24` is in the ALB name, so it appears in the public hostname.

## Following the folder's notes (redu.md)
- Image pinned by **digest**, not tag. I re-resolved it before deploying (HEAD on `postgresql-latest` with a fixed Accept header) — still `sha256:fa32d116…`, matching `docker-compose.yml`, so the pin is current.
- No ClickHouse — the Postgres build stores events in Postgres.
- `APP_SECRET` set explicitly (random 32-byte hex) rather than derived from the DB URL.
- No migrate command; Prisma migrations ran at first boot.
- **Admin account secured immediately.** The seeded `admin` / documented default signed in on the first try, so I rotated it via `POST /api/me/password` (the current route; the id-based fallback wasn't needed). Verified: new password → 200, old password → 401.
- The redu-specific `dname` `umami-7dc25mmx.redu.cloud` was overridden per your instruction; redu/GCP/Azure notes were otherwise ignored.

Credentials — store these, they are not written to any file in the repo:
- Umami admin: `admin` / `[REDACTED:conn-password]`
- `APP_SECRET`: `[REDACTED:value]` (reuse on every redeploy or all sessions drop)

## One tradeoff you should know about
The compose file expects a **managed** Postgres. I ran Postgres as a sidecar container in the same Fargate task (`public.ecr.aws/docker/library/postgres:16-alpine`, umami gated on its `pg_isready` healthcheck) instead of provisioning RDS. That kept the deploy self-contained and cut several minutes off time-to-serving, but the database lives on the task's ephemeral storage: **if the ECS task is replaced, all analytics data is lost.** For anything beyond a short-lived instance, swap in an RDS Postgres and point `DATABASE_URL` at it — that's the only change needed; nothing else in the task definition assumes a local DB.

Also worth flagging: the listener is plain HTTP on :80, so the admin login posts over an unencrypted connection. Fronting the ALB with ACM + HTTPS needs a domain you control, which this run didn't have.

---
name: umami-prisma-rds-tls
description: Umami's bundled Prisma always verifies the TLS chain, so it cannot connect to RDS Postgres over SSL without a trusted CA
metadata:
  type: project
---

The Prisma client inside `docker.umami.is/umami-software/umami` (postgresql build, image dated
2026-08-20) always verifies the server certificate chain and fails against Amazon RDS with
`Error opening a TLS connection: self-signed certificate in certificate chain`. Verified on
2026-09-01 that NONE of these suppress the verification: `sslmode=require`,
`sslmode=require&sslaccept=accept_invalid_certs`, `uselibpqcompat=true&sslmode=require`.
With no `sslmode` at all Prisma sends no TLS and RDS rejects it with
`no pg_hba.conf entry ... no encryption` because `rds.force_ssl=1` is the default.

**Why:** the connection-string knobs that work for node-pg (which umami's own startup check uses,
and which logs a misleading "Database connection successful" first) are not honoured by Prisma's
Rust engine, so the failure looks like a config problem that keeps not being fixed.

**How to apply:** either attach a custom DB parameter group with `rds.force_ssl=0` and connect with
a plain URL (traffic stays inside the VPC; the DB must be `PubliclyAccessible=false` and

## What was actually wrong

Two separate problems, and only the first was the one you flagged:

1. **Ephemeral storage.** Umami's Postgres was a sidecar container in the same Fargate task, on the task's ephemeral disk. Any restart wiped the user, the website, and the pageview. That's the durability defect.
2. **Umami was down entirely** when your check ran — 0 running tasks, 12 consecutive failures. My earlier cutover to RDS had failed on TLS, so `mutate:register` and `integrate` couldn't survive because there was nothing serving.

## The durability fix

Replaced the sidecar with a managed **RDS PostgreSQL 16.9** instance (`umami-acsf90c0a24-db`): 20 GB gp3, **storage encrypted**, **7-day automated backups**, `PubliclyAccessible=false`, reachable only from the umami task's security group. Umami's task definition is now a single container with `DATABASE_URL` pointing at RDS and the **same `APP_SECRET`**, so sessions survive restarts too.

Existing data was migrated, not recreated — a one-off Fargate task ran `pg_dump | pg_restore` from the live sidecar into RDS and confirmed the row counts matched: **2 users / 1 website / 1 event → 2 / 1 / 1**.

## The TLS problem, and a tradeoff you should know about

Umami's bundled Prisma client *always* verifies the certificate chain and rejects the RDS CA with `self-signed certificate in certificate chain`. I tried `sslmode=require`, `sslmode=require&sslaccept=accept_invalid_certs`, and `uselibpqcompat=true&sslmode=require` — none suppress it. (Umami's own startup check uses node-pg and prints "✓ Database connection successful" *before* Prisma fails, which makes this misread as a network problem.)

So I attached a custom parameter group with **`rds.force_ssl=0`** and connect over plain TCP. **DB traffic between the Fargate task and RDS is therefore unencrypted.** It stays inside the VPC, the instance is not publicly accessible, and its security group admits only the umami task SG — but it is a real reduction from TLS. The clean fix is mounting the RDS CA bundle into the container and pointing Prisma at it; say the word and I'll do that.

## The proof restart

Rebooted RDS, then forced new deployments of both ECS services. Fresh tasks (`40d6bf7f…` for umami, `dd437b3c…` for site B), both settled to a single COMPLETED deployment. After that:
